inlines.v: CONDUIT, noun [Latin , to conduct.] 1. A canal or pipe for the conveyance of water; an aqueduct. Conduits are made of lead, stone, cast iron, wood, etc., above or below the surface of the earth. 2. A vessel that conveys the blood or other fluid. The conduits of my blood. 3. A conductor. These organs are the nerves which are the conduits to convey them from without to their audience in the brain. 4. A pipe or cock for drawing off liquor. 5. Any channel that conveys water or fluids; a sink, sewer or drain.
